Test and stopping rules

Source: R/ms_test.R
ms_test.Rd

Defines the one-sided log-rank test, the efficacy and futility bounds and the approximation of the distribution of the statistics.

Usage

ms_test(
  alpha = 0.025,
  endpoints = "os",
  sf_eff = "OF",
  param_eff = NULL,
  futility = c("none", "fixed", "beta"),
  fut_bound = NULL,
  fut_scale = c("z", "hr"),
  sf_fut = "OF",
  param_fut = NULL,
  beta = 0.1,
  binding = FALSE,
  mean = c("direct", "schoenfeld"),
  variance = c("null", "alternative", "studentized"),
  spending_time = c("events", "information"),
  mtp = c("none", "bonferroni", "fixed_sequence"),
  weights = NULL,
  hierarchical = c("overall", "stagewise")
)

Arguments

alpha

One-sided type I error (with two endpoints, the familywise error rate).

endpoints

Tested endpoint, "os" or "pfs", or both in the order of testing (for example c("pfs", "os")). With two endpoints the futility bounds are placed on the first, and with mtp = "fixed_sequence" the first is tested first.

sf_eff, param_eff

Alpha spending function and its parameter (see gs_spend). For "user", param_eff gives the cumulative proportions of alpha at the looks. With two endpoints, sf_eff has one value or one value per endpoint, and param_eff is a list with one element per endpoint, or a number or one number per endpoint.

futility

"none", "fixed" or "beta" (for the first endpoint).

fut_bound

Fixed futility bounds at the interim looks (for futility = "fixed").

fut_scale

Scale of fut_bound: "z" or "hr".

sf_fut, param_fut

Beta spending function and its parameter.

beta

Total type II error for beta spending in ms_power; ms_size uses one minus the target power instead.

binding

Whether the futility bounds are binding.

mean

Approximation of the mean of the statistic: "direct" or "schoenfeld" (see lr_moments).

variance

Approximation of the covariance of the statistics: "null", "alternative" or "studentized" (see lr_cov).

spending_time

"events" or "information".

mtp

Multiple testing procedure: "none" (one endpoint), "bonferroni" or "fixed_sequence" (two endpoints).

weights

Bonferroni weights of the two endpoints (positive, adding up to 1; defaults to equal weights).

hierarchical

"overall" or "stagewise" (for mtp = "fixed_sequence").

Value

An object of class ms_test.

Details

The efficacy bounds are obtained by alpha spending under the null hypothesis. The correlation of the statistics under the null hypothesis is taken as sqrt(d_j / d_k), where d are the expected numbers of events of the tested endpoint at the looks; it is exact under the null hypothesis when the looks are driven by the events of the tested endpoint. The spending time is the event fraction (spending_time = "events") or the information fraction under the design scenario ("information").

Futility bounds may be fixed, on the Z scale (fut_scale = "z") or on the hazard ratio scale (fut_scale = "hr", converted with z = -log(hr) sqrt(p0 p1 d)), or obtained by beta spending under the design scenario. With binding = FALSE the efficacy bounds ignore the futility bounds.

With two endpoints, each endpoint has its own efficacy bounds, computed as above from the looks at which it is tested (see ms_looks). With mtp = "bonferroni", the endpoint k is tested at level weights[k] * alpha; the levels are not recycled after a rejection. With mtp = "fixed_sequence", both endpoints are tested at level alpha and the second endpoint is tested only after the first has been rejected: with hierarchical = "overall" at the analysis at which the first is rejected and at its later looks until it is rejected (procedure (b) of Glimm et al. 2010), and with "stagewise" only at the analysis at which the first is rejected, where the trial stops (procedure (a) of Glimm et al. 2010, Tamhane et al. 2010). The bounds of the second endpoint do not depend on the correlation between the endpoints; with them the familywise error rate is at most alpha (Glimm et al. 2010, Tamhane et al. 2010). Futility bounds are placed on the first endpoint only: the trial stops when its statistic falls below the futility bound at an interim look at which it has not been rejected. See gs_prob_mtp for the stopping rules.

The efficacy bounds and the non-binding type I error (with two endpoints, the familywise error rate under the global null hypothesis) do not depend on variance; the power, the futility bounds by beta spending and the familywise error rate under null_scenarios of ms_power do. In the simulations of inst/validation/ with PFS and OS tested together, the powers with "null" and "studentized" agreed with the simulated powers within the Monte Carlo error, "alternative" gave slightly larger powers, and "studentized" agreed best with the simulated standard deviations and correlations of the statistics.

References

Glimm E, Maurer W, Bretz F (2010). Hierarchical testing of multiple endpoints in group-sequential trials. Statistics in Medicine 29:219-228.

Tamhane AC, Mehta CR, Liu L (2010). Testing a primary and a secondary endpoint in a group sequential design. Biometrics 66:1174-1184.

See also

ms_power, gs_bounds, gs_prob_mtp

Examples

ms_test()
#> One-sided log-rank test of OS at level 0.025
#>   Efficacy: alpha spending "OF"
#>   Futility: none
#>   Mean: "direct"; variance: "null"; spending time: "events"
ms_test(futility = "beta", sf_fut = "HSD", param_fut = -2)
#> One-sided log-rank test of OS at level 0.025
#>   Efficacy: alpha spending "OF"
#>   Futility: beta spending "HSD" with beta = 0.1 (non-binding)
#>   Mean: "direct"; variance: "null"; spending time: "events"
ms_test(futility = "fixed", fut_bound = 1, fut_scale = "hr")
#> One-sided log-rank test of OS at level 0.025
#>   Efficacy: alpha spending "OF"
#>   Futility: fixed bounds on the hazard ratio scale (1) (non-binding)
#>   Mean: "direct"; variance: "null"; spending time: "events"
# PFS first, then OS, with Pocock-type spending for OS
ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), sf_eff = c("OF", "Pocock"),
        mtp = "fixed_sequence")
#> One-sided log-rank tests of PFS and OS at familywise level 0.025
#>   Fixed sequence: PFS, then OS (overall)
#>   Efficacy: alpha spending "OF" (PFS), "Pocock" (OS)
#>   Futility (PFS): none
#>   Mean: "direct"; variance: "null"; spending time: "events"
ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), mtp = "bonferroni", weights = c(0.8, 0.2))
#> One-sided log-rank tests of PFS and OS at familywise level 0.025
#>   Bonferroni: PFS at level 0.02, OS at level 0.005
#>   Efficacy: alpha spending "OF" (PFS), "OF" (OS)
#>   Futility (PFS): none
#>   Mean: "direct"; variance: "null"; spending time: "events"
